25 An electromagnetic wave in free space has a frequency of 3.0  1016
Hz.
Which row gives the principal region of this wave and an example of an electromagnetic wave
with a lower frequency?
principal region
wave with lower
frequency
A
infrared
visible light
B
infrared
X-rays
C
ultraviolet
visible light
D
ultraviolet
X-rays

hints: Notice the given value $3.0 \times 10^{16} \text{ Hz}$ and compare it with the familiar visible light frequencies near $4 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ to $7 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.
Recall the spectrum in order of increasing frequency: infrared, then visible light, then ultraviolet, then X-rays.
Use $c = f\lambda$ to check the wavelength of the $3.0 \times 10^{16} \text{ Hz}$ wave, then decide which named wave in the table must lie below it in frequency.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: $f = 3.0 \times 10^{16} \text{ Hz}$ in free space, where all electromagnetic waves travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8} \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Recall the frequency order: infrared is below visible light, visible light is about $10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, ultraviolet is about $10^{15} \text{ Hz}$ to $10^{17} \text{ Hz}$, and X-rays are above that.
Check by wavelength: $\lambda = c/f = 3.0 \times 10^{8} / 3.0 \times 10^{16} = 1.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ m}$, which is $10 \text{ nm}$ and lies in the ultraviolet region, not infrared.
Compare the second column: visible light at $\sim 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ is lower in frequency than $3.0 \times 10^{16} \text{ Hz}$, while X-rays at $>10^{17} \text{ Hz}$ are higher in frequency.
Therefore the principal region is ultraviolet and the lower-frequency example is visible light. This is option C

A.explanation: Infrared is incorrect because its frequencies are about $10^{12} \text{ Hz}$ to $4 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, far below $3.0 \times 10^{16} \text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: Infrared is the wrong region, and X-rays have higher frequency than $3.0 \times 10^{16} \text{ Hz}$, not lower.

C.explanation: $3.0 \times 10^{16} \text{ Hz}$ lies in the ultraviolet region, and visible light at about $10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ has a lower frequency.

D.explanation: Ultraviolet is the correct region, but X-rays have higher frequency than ultraviolet, so they are not lower in frequency.
